grupo1.q1: What is the Hybrid architecture (Local-First + Cloud)?
grupo1.a1: A modern architecture is used. Your working data (students, grades) is processed locally in your browser, guaranteeing total privacy and speed. Heavy operations (PDF report generation or connection with Artificial Intelligence) rely securely on a central server.
grupo1.a2: The data from your Curriculum Plan and your Courses resides in your own browser (IndexedDB). You have absolute control over it. For security, it's recommended to frequently use file export (BYOC) from the Files tab.
grupo1.q3: What's the difference between 'Curriculum Plan' and 'Course'?
grupo1.a3: It's a vital concept: the 'Curriculum Plan' is your theoretical template; it contains the letter of the law (learning outcomes, assessment criteria) and your teaching units (reusable year after year). The 'Course' is the real instance; it represents an actual group of flesh-and-blood students in a specific school year, with their grades and absences.
grupo1.q4: What happens if I delete my browser's data or cache?
grupo1.a4: If you clear your browser's deep cache without having exported your data beforehand, you will lose your work. That's why it's vital to periodically use the 'Export' button to save your progress to a .json file, keeping local backups.
grupo1.q5: Can I work from multiple computers?
grupo1.a5: Yes. To transfer your environment between your school computer and your personal laptop, just 'Export' your progress on computer A and click 'Import' on computer B.

grupo2.q1: Do I have to manually enter all the RA and CE from the BOE?
grupo2.a1: No! The system includes an official Catalog that automatically imports the legal regulations (learning outcomes and criteria) for your module. You just need to choose your Grade and your Training Cycle in the initial Catalog section, and the system does it for you.
grupo2.q2: What does it mean that the RA don't add up to 100% in the checks?
grupo2.a2: For the continuous mathematical assessment to work, each Learning Outcome (RA) must have a 'weight' or level of importance. The total sum of the weights of all the RA in a module must be exactly 100%. You need to adjust this in Curriculum Plan > Curriculum > 'RA and CE' tab.
grupo2.q3: How do I configure the hours students spend at the company (Dual FP)?
grupo2.a3: In Curriculum Plan > Context > 'Identification' tab, choose whether your arrangement is General Dual, Intensive Dual, or None. Then, in Curriculum Plan > Context > 'FEOE and dual arrangement' tab, describe how that in-company training is organized and tracked. To mark which specific Learning Outcomes are dual, go to Curriculum Plan > Curriculum > 'RA and CE' tab.
grupo2.q4: What is the EQAVET section for?
grupo2.a4: It's used to integrate the European continuous-improvement cycle into your curriculum plan. You'll find it under 'Home' > 'Improvement' tab. At the end of the year, you self-assess the quality indicators and note your improvement proposals for the following year. The teaching self-assessment rubric follows ANECA's DOCENTIA model (see aneca.es/docentia), adapted to FP practice.
grupo2.q5: What's the difference between complementary and extracurricular activities?
grupo2.a5: They are legally distinct: complementary activities take place within teaching hours, are linked to the curriculum, and are gradable — they are part of your didactic curriculum plan. Extracurricular activities take place outside school hours, are voluntary, and are never gradable — they go in the centre's PGA, not in the PD; in Methodology > Cross-curricular you can still note them for reference, but they don't count in the curriculum plan.
grupo2.q6: What's the difference between an assessment instrument and a grading instrument?
grupo2.a6: For each Assessment Criterion (CE) there are two distinct things: the assessment instrument is the activity that generates the evidence (an objective test, a task, an oral defence...), and the grading instrument is what scores that evidence (a rubric, a scale, a checklist...). In Instruments you can code both separately when configuring each instrument.

grupo3.titulo: 3. Step 3: Creating the course and roster
grupo3.q1: Can I import students from platforms like Séneca, Rayuela, or an Excel file?
grupo3.a1: Yes. In the 'Students' section you can import a CSV (Excel) file with your class list. Alternatively, the smart table lets you copy and paste cells in bulk, just like a spreadsheet.
grupo3.q2: What level of security does my students' data have?
grupo3.a2: Your local files never leave for our server unless you want them to (using 'Save Locally'). If you choose to save them to Google Drive or OneDrive, the file is transmitted directly between your browser and Microsoft/Google's servers. You can enable local encryption so the file is completely unreadable without your master key.
grupo3.q3: Is the application protected against hacking or outages?
grupo3.a3: Yes. The frontend includes a Content Security Policy (CSP) that blocks code-injection attacks (XSS) to protect your local data. In addition, our server has 'Rate Limiting' (request throttling) that prevents denial-of-service attacks (DDoS), ensuring the official catalogs are always available when you need them.
grupo3.q4: How do I physically arrange students in the classroom?
grupo3.a4: Inside 'Students' you'll find a 'Classroom layout' tab. It's a visual, interactive board where you can drag and drop students onto their respective desks to get the exact layout of your class.
grupo3.q5: How do I use the Dropout Alerts system?
grupo3.a5: The early-prevention panel lets you record calls to families, disciplinary reports, or referrals to the guidance department for students at risk of dropping out.

grupo4.a1: It's your daily logbook. It lets you note what happens in each actual class session: which UD you covered, whether there were any incidents, or mark 'No teaching' days (such as strikes or staff meetings) so they don't count toward your progress.
grupo4.q2: How is the 'Monthly planning' forecast calculated?
grupo4.a2: It's calculated day by day using the holiday calendar and the weekly timetable you already have registered in the app — it's not a proportional estimate, it's an exact calculation from that data. It will change if the official school-year calendar or the final timetable distribution are not yet complete.
grupo4.q3: How do I take attendance or record absences?
grupo4.a3: In the Tracking section you have the 'Attendance' tab. You'll see all your students, and with a single click on their grid cell you can toggle between Absence, Late, or Justified Absence.
grupo4.q4: How do I grade a specific task or exam?
grupo4.a4: Go to the 'Tracking' section > 'Detail by student' tab to enter the grade for each activity, per student. The final grade is automatically recalculated from the RA and CE weights.
grupo4.q5: How exactly is the term's final grade calculated?
grupo4.a5: The system cross-references the grades you enter in the Instruments with the weight of the Indicator (Assessment > Indicators block), which in turn feeds the weight of the Assessment Criterion (CE) and finally the Learning Outcome (RA). All in real time.
grupo4.q6: What do the colors (purple, teal, orange) mean in the agenda and visual calendar?
grupo4.a6: The background colors indicate which term (assessment period) each activity or date belongs to: 1st term (purple/mauve), 2nd term (teal), and 3rd term (orange/amber) — deliberately without red or blue, as those tones are reserved for Holiday and Event.

grupo5.q1: Can I generate automatic report cards for students?
grupo5.a1: Yes. From the 'Course' tab in MagIA, you can generate bulk PDF report cards for the whole class, or hyper-detailed individual summaries that justify the grade based on each Assessment Criterion achieved.

grupo7.q1: What happens if the charts on my dashboard don't load?
grupo7.a1: Check in the sidebar that you have enabled 'Real Mode' and have your Group selected. The charts need to know which students and which curriculum plan to point to in order to analyze the data.
grupo7.q2: Can Cuaderno FP be used on a mobile phone?
grupo7.a2: The design is responsive and adapts, but due to the density of information (large assessment tables and curriculum matrices), we strongly recommend using it on computer screens or large tablets.
grupo7.q3: The app is very slow, or I've noticed a strange error
grupo7.a3: Try reloading the page completely (F5 or Ctrl+R). If the error keeps appearing, export your data (.json) immediately to keep it safe, and contact support detailing the steps to reproduce your problem.
